mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of tightening (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening economy, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity, measured by housing starts, indicates a strengthening economy, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising housing starts (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of declining industrial production (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong payroll growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between rising real GDP and falling unemployment rate signals a robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDP growth and falling unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% in a month, coupled with a federal funds rate below 2%, indicates inflationary pressure without sufficient monetary tightening, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high inflation and low interest rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales by more than 1% in a month signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising retail sales (t-test p > 0.05).
